problem_statement.flow_justification_note: CuAAC in a Cu/C packed-bed cartridge (CatCart) is a well-established flow motif: the heterogeneous catalyst is already formatted as a cartridge, the 0.3 mL reactor volume maps directly to sub-minute residence times at pump-accessible flow rates, and the 20 bar BPR keeps acetone liquid well above its boiling point (56 °C) at 150 °C. Flow eliminates the need for a microwave and provides continuous throughput with improved heat and mass transfer through the packed bed.
ambiguities: Catalyst loading in the CatCart (wt% Cu, bed void fraction, and bed density) is not specified; 10 mol% Cu relative to substrate is the batch figure but the cartridge has a fixed Cu inventory — actual mol% Cu delivered per pass is unknown without cartridge specifications.

Acetone boiling point is 56 °C; at 150 °C and 20 bar the system is well above Tb but vapour pressure of acetone at 150 °C (~8–9 bar) is safely below 20 bar BPR setpoint — assumed adequate to keep liquid phase, but this should be verified against the exact Antoine constants.

No mixer is listed in the inventory; it is assumed the two reagents (benzyl azide and phenylacetylene) are pre-mixed in a single stock solution before loading into the pump reservoir, avoiding the need for a T-mixer.

Benzyl azide is an energetic material; the blast shield is listed but no secondary containment volume or pressure rating is given — assumed adequate for the small scale (≤1 mL total azide in system at any time).

The packed-bed void fraction is assumed ~0.4 (typical for granular Cu/C), giving an interstitial (liquid) volume of ~0.12 mL and a total bed volume of 0.3 mL; residence time calculations use the total reactor volume as a conservative upper bound.
No inline analytics (UV, IR) are listed; conversion will be assessed offline by TLC or HPLC on collected fractions.
The single HPLC pump limits the system to a pre-mixed feed; if separate reagent streams are later desired, a second pump would be required.
Stainless steel compatibility with benzyl azide at 150 °C is assumed acceptable for short contact times; prolonged storage of azide solutions in SS should be avoided.
The vented collection vessel (max 1 bar) is downstream of the BPR, so it sees only atmospheric pressure — confirmed safe.

Estimated flow residence time of 0.3 min is a model hypothesis matching the batch microwave time; actual conversion at this residence time is unvalidated and is the primary unknown driving SCREEN disposition.

Scientific rationale: CuAAC [3+2] cycloaddition of benzyl azide with phenylacetylene over heterogeneous Cu/C CatCart. Rate-limiting step is metalacycle formation at the Cu surface. chemistry_notes.text: CuAAC [3+2] cycloaddition of benzyl azide with phenylacetylene over heterogeneous Cu/C CatCart. Rate-limiting step is metalacycle formation at the Cu surface. Flow advantage: packed-bed provides continuous intimate substrate-catalyst contact, eliminating diffusion limitation present in batch. Acetone bp = 56 degC; at 150 degC operating temperature, vapour pressure ~11.3 bar, so 20 bar BPR (only available setpoint) is mandatory and sufficient. The 4 mm ID CatCart is larger than ideal for plug-flow (Pe ~4, significant axial dispersion per calculations); this is accepted as the only available reactor. Residence time is set to 0.6 min (0.3 mL / 0.5 mL/min) as a starting screen point; a residence time screen from 0.1 to 1.0 mL/min (0.3-3 min) is recommended. Benzyl azide must be handled dilute (0.25 M) and behind blast shield at all times. Cu leaching from CatCart into product stream is a known risk and should be monitored by ICP-MS. No deoxygenation required. No light source required or available.
